title: AAFP and ISFM Feline Environmental Needs Guidelines
excerpt: Published in Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery (2013), these guidelines from the American Association of Feline Practitioners and International Society of Feline Medicine state that cats require access to vertical space including perches, shelves, and climbing opportunities. The guidelines note that vertical territory is essential for cats to feel secure, allows establishment of hierarchy without direct confrontation, and significantly reduces inter-cat tension in multi-cat households.

title: A critically appraised topic (CAT) to compare the effects of single and multi-cat housing on physiological and behavioural measures of stress in domestic cats in confined environments
excerpt: Published in BMC Veterinary Research (2014) by Finka, Ellis, and Stavisky. This systematic review examined stress measures in single vs. multi-cat housing. The study identified environmental enrichment including vertical space as a key mediator of stress. Authors concluded that when adequate resources including vertical territory are provided, multi-cat housing does not increase stress and may allow for natural social behaviors while reducing competition through spatial distribution.

title: Environmental enrichment for cats - International Cat Care
excerpt: International Cat Care (a respected veterinary organization) states that cats feel safer when they can climb to elevated positions. Vertical space is particularly critical in multi-cat homes as it allows cats to establish territories at different heights, provides escape routes from potential conflicts, and reduces direct competition for floor-level resources. The resource recommends cat trees, wall shelves, and window perches as essential enrichment.
